UCI World Championships Men’s Individual Time-Trial 2026: Our form guide

The time-trials kick off proceedings at the 2026 UCI World Championships, which are being held in Montreal, Canada. The men’s elite ITT is 39.2km in length over a flat course with just 220m of elevation, traversing and crossing the St. Lawrence River to end back where they started with a slight uphill kick towards the Avenue du Parc.

Last year, Remco Evenepoel (Belgium) took the crown on a 40.6km route ahead of Jay Vine (Australia) and Ilan Van Wilder (Belgium). Evenepoel is back in Canada looking for number four and should see his closest competition from Filippo Ganna (Italy) and Stefan Küng (Switzerland).

Remco Evenepoel (Belgium)

Defending champion Remco Evenepoel is eyeing a fourth consecutive victory in the individual time-trial. Truly one of the greatest time-triallists of all time, the 26-year-old somehow only seems to get stronger in the discipline. He has four individual wins in a time-trial this year including a Tour de France stage. It’s looking likely he’ll don the rainbow bands for another year.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st place x 3 (Volta Comunitat Valenciana, UAE Tour, Tour de France)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 1st (2023, 2024, 2025)

Filippo Ganna (Italy)

Filippo Ganna knows a thing or two about time-trials. The Hour record holder has utterly dominated his National Championships with five consecutive victories but last won a world title in 2021. Since then, he finished seventh in 2022 and then second behind Evenepoel in 2023 and 2024.

This year Ganna has won time-trials at the Volta ao Algarve, Tirreno-Adriatico and the Giro d’Italia, but Evenepoel was not present for any of them, and he could only manage 11th in the Tour TT.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st place x 4 (Volta ao Algarve, Tirreno Adriatico, Giro d’Italia, Italian National Championships)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 1st (2020, 2021)

Stefan Küng (Switzerland)

A World Championship is missing from Stefan Küng’s palmarès, with National and European titles already in the bag. His best Worlds placing came in 2022 when he finished second. Last year he finished tenth in Rwanda.

After spending most of the season out injured, Küng has been in strong TT form since his return, winning tests against the clock at the Tour de Pologne and then at the Vuelta. A a podium is realistic for the Swiss rider.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st x 2 (Tour de Pologne, Vuelta a España)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 2nd (2022)

Isaac del Toro (Mexico)

Isaac del Toro doesn’t tend to be thought of for his time-trialling, however he finished fifth at Worlds last year, and has had a few top showings against the clock this season too with fifth in the Tour TT and a victory in the prologue at the Lidl Deutschland Tour. He could be a sneaky outsider for the podium, but his head will likely be more focused on the road race.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st (Prologue, Lidl Deutschland Tour)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 5th (2025)

Paul Seixas (France)

Paul Seixas won the Junior World Championships TT in 2024, and last year rode the elite time-trial desepite being just 18. The Frenchman has captivated the cycling world this season, and arrives in Montréal with a real chance at a rainbow jersey in the road race.

In TTs this season he won at Itzulia Basque Country and finished fourth in the Tour TT. He has a shot at a medal here.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st (Itzulia Basque Country)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 1st (2024, Junior)

Ethan Hayter (Great Britain)

Ethan Hayter came incredibly close to winning the opening stage time-trial at the Vuelta, just missing out to Pogačar by nine hundredths of a second. That’s likely delivered some extra end-of-season motivation. It might be a bit too long for the British Time-Trial Champion’s strengths, looking stronger in the Vuelta shorter test, but he finished just off the podium in 2022 on a 34km course.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st (National Time-Trial Championships)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 4th (2022)

Callum Thornley (Great Britain)

Callum Thornley is Britain’s next great time-trial talent. The 23-year-old Scot is only in his first pro season but had an impressive Vuelta, finishing fourth on the Stage 1 time-trial and second to Küng by just two seconds on the longer Stage 18 TT. With that form, a famous medal could be on the cards.

  • Best ITT result this season: 2nd (Vuelta a España)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 5th (2025, U23)

Tobias Foss (Netherlands)

Tobias Foss shocked the world when he claimed the rainbow jersey in 2022. Not that his time-trialling isn’t good, rather the competition was so fierce. This season, Foss won the Norwegian ITT Championship, raced to third in the time-trial at the Tour de Suisse and, while Netcompany Ineos finished second in the TTT at the Tour, he failed to leave his mark in the ITT with a 42nd place.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st (National Time-Trial Championships)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 1st (2022)

Daan Hoole (Netherlands)

Daan Hoole has only raced in two individual time-trials this season. The Dutchman came fifth in the UAE Tour but 17th at the Tour, though that was a hilly course.

The 27-year-old has a massive engine and won his first Grand Tour stage at the Giro’s ITT last season. He should finish in the top ten.

  • Best ITT result this season: 5th (UAE Tour)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 17th (2024)

Mathias Vacek (Czech Republic)

Czech Republic’s double national champion, Mathias Vacek powered to third on the time-trial at the Volta Comunitat Valenciana, fourth at the Tour de Suisse and notched a win at the ZLM Tour this season.

He’s a former Junior European Champion in the discipline and will be looking to improve on his 27th place at the elite level in 2024.

  • Best ITT result this season: 5th (UAE Tour)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 9th (2022, U23)
